records.label: Chan Chan urban core and urban population estimate
rejection_reasons: Schaedel's 70,000-105,000 estimate is explicitly the urban population of the Chimor state, including approximately 50,000-75,000 in Chan Chan; it is not a rural local-food boundary.
Chan Chan's capital primacy, specialization and state tribute make it precisely the kind of city/trade hub that cannot supervise surrounding intrinsic land capacity.
The same source gives a separate 500,000-750,000 demographic hinterland envelope; the urban interval must not be added to or substituted for that regional boundary.
records.notes: Retain for a diagnostic of how much an urban capital can exceed local cell food capacity, never as a training target.

records.label: Quebrada del Oso Chimú agricultural production centre
rejection_reasons: Tavera-Medina et al. identify an approximately 60 ha site with fields, an administrative compound and evidence of maize/beans, canal water and fourteenth-century field expansion, but publish no defensible population or carrying-capacity interval for the site.
The study describes a workforce and relocated populations associated with a state canal project; that is an agricultural-production test, not an equilibrium population label.
A 60 ha archaeological centre cannot be expanded to the entire Chicama or Chan Chan province without an independently reconstructed rural boundary.
records.notes: Keep as a qualitative/physical irrigation validation case. The new Chimor eleven-valley packet is the only regional mapping candidate from this evidence family.

records.label: Pacbitun Late Classic Maya regional centre
rejection_reasons: Healy et al. estimate approximately 5,000-6,000 people in the 9 km2 Pacbitun site (with a table total near 6,850), and density of 550-950 persons/km2 across core and periphery; this is a medium-sized civic centre, not a regional rural boundary.

The settlement's terraces and population growth provide pressure evidence, but no independent saturation fraction or local-food accounting separates residents from exchange and political support networks.
The Late Classic date is far outside the 1337 target and the EU5 map has no Pacbitun-specific polygon.
records.notes: Retain as a negative control for the city-versus-hinterland distinction and for terrace/soil pressure features.

records.label: Ancestral Pueblo Pajarito/Jemez Plateau drought-population sequence
rejection_reasons: The Jemez/Pajarito study combines two small plateau study areas (8.47 and 8.31 km2) and momentary-mean site estimates; it reports a Pajarito decline from approximately 6,000 to 2,000, plus a 32% decline during AD 1350-1400 drought, rather than a stable regional population interval.
Water-cost and drought evidence is excellent for physical stress testing, but migration, dual residence and later aggregation prevent a clean Malthusian saturation interpretation.
The published study polygons do not have a verified one-to-one EU5 selector, so no aggregate score is allowed.
records.notes: Use the drought/water-cost relationships as a physical validation fixture once the study polygons are mapped; do not fit a population scale to this sequence.

records.label: Rurutu wetland-taro landscape carrying-capacity study
rejection_reasons: Escue and Kahn identify 20 dormant taro systems covering 138.3 ha and model probable yield/carrying-capacity distributions, but explicitly state that precise pre-contact population estimates are lacking and that their results are preliminary.
The island has a strong local-food and warfare/land-pressure signal, but the current EU5 geometry has no verified Rurutu tag or crosswalk, so the boundary cannot be scored.
Post-contact depopulation and later imported-food exchange make the surviving modern terraces an unsafe direct proxy for 1337 saturation.
records.notes: Retain the 38.2 km2 island, terrace, fallow and warfare evidence in the research queue; no population interval is invented.

records.label: Pre-contact Caribbean genetic effective-population estimates
rejection_reasons: Fernandes et al. estimate effective population size (Ne), not census population: minimum approximately 500-1,500 and maximum approximately 1,530-8,150 for combined Puerto Rico and Hispaniola genetic lineages.
Ne cannot be converted to people supported by local food without a demographic model, and the combined-island genetic boundary is not a mappable historical food region.
No independent archaeological saturation or pressure interval is attached; using the genetic number as a population target would create a false low label.
records.notes: Keep only as a cautionary demographic-genetics comparison; never use Ne as a census or carrying-capacity label.
